problem:
Consider the following differential equation.

$$
6{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+x(6x+1){y}^{′}+y=0
$$

Which of the following is a Frobenius series solution to the differential equation given above, where ${a}_{n}$ for $n=0,1,2,…$ are constants determined by substitution?

*Hint: Substituting a trial Frobenius series solution into each term of the ODE, we obtain*

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}{y}^{″} & =6({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda ){a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+6{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }((\lambda +n)^{2}-(\lambda +n)){a}_{n}{x}^{\lambda +n}, \\ x(6x+1){y}^{′} & =\lambda {a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }[6(\lambda +n-1){a}_{n-1}+(\lambda +n){a}_{n}]{x}^{\lambda +n}, \\ y & ={a}_{0}{x}^{\lambda }+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}{x}^{\lambda +n}.\end{aligned}
$$
